newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian party candidates cleared of wrong-doing.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian party candidates cleared of wrong-doing.

text.p: Candidates vying for posts in Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's party have been cleared of campaign irregularities, a top party official said on Monday.

Investigations into more than 100 allegations against some of the 185 candidates vying for posts in the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) have not turned up any proof to disqualify any candidate, party Secretary General Mohamed Rahmat told a news conference.
"There is not one concrete case which would cause disqualification," he said.
Nine candidates had voluntarily withdrawn from their races, he added.
UMNO, lynchpin of Malaysia's ruling National Front coalition, will hold its triennial elections on October 9-12.
Mohamed said last week that the official list of candidates had been delayed to allow the completion of investigations into reports of vote buying and other campaign transgressions.
Mahathir had decreed a total ban on campaigning last month, citing the need for party unity and fears that candidates were blatantly buying votes.
Mahathir was automatically re-elected as president and deputy prime minister Anwar Ibrahim as his deputy, both unopposed. UMNO agreed last year there would be no contest for the top two jobs.

By convention, the president and deputy president also occupy the posts of prime minister and deputy prime minister. Thus, many political analysts view the triennial UMNO elections as more significant than a general election.
The UMNO-dominated National Front coalition has ruled Malaysia since independence from Britain nearly 40 years ago, and it has won all elections since by landslides.

All other posts are up for grabs, including the three vice-presidencies, the heads of the youth and women's wings of the party and 25 positions on the Supreme Council, the policy making arm of the party.
